34 Financial instruments (continued) (b) Valuation of financial instruments - valuation hierarchy The following table presents the Group's financial assets and financial liabilities measured and recognised at fair value, by level of fair value hierarchy: • Level 1, quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities that can be accessed at the measurement date; • Level 2, inputs other than quoted prices included within Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly; and • Level 3, inputs for the asset or liability that are not based on observable market data (that is, unobservable inputs). Level 2 assets are valued by discounting future cash flows using externally sourced market yield curves, including interest rate curves and foreign exchange rates from highly liquid markets. For level 3 assets and liabilities: • The fair value of investment funds is measured using the latest net asset value of the fund available as at the balance sheet date; and • For the Group's investments in unquoted entities, where there are often no current earnings, no short- term future earnings or positive cash flows, it is often difficult to make reliable cash flow forecasts. The Group also consider that fair value estimates based entirely on observable market data are of greater reliability than those based on assumptions. Given these circumstances, the price of the most recent investment event is typically considered to be the best input to derive fair value at the date of investment. As a result, the price of the most recent investment event, by the Group or a third party, is typically used as the de facto starting position for any fair value assessment made by the Group, after taking into account the following factors: – the period of time for which it remains appropriate to use the price of the most recent investment; and – a company's equity structure, especially where it involves different class rights in a sale or liquidity event. On November 11, 2026 the Board of Directors (the "Board") of Marvell Technology, Inc. (the "Company") approved an increase in the size of the Board from seven (7) to ten (10) members and the appointments of Donna C. Morris, Douglas R. Bettinger and Sasan K. Goodarzi to the Board, in each case effective November 12, 2026. Ms. Morris and Mr. Goodarzi have been appointed to the Executive Compensation Committee of the Board, and Mr. Bettinger has been appointed to the Audit Committee of the Board. Each of Ms. Morris, Mr. Bettinger and Mr. Goodarzi will stand for election at the Company's 2027 annual meeting of stockholders. The Board has determined that each of Ms. Morris, Mr. Bettinger and Mr. Goodarzi is an "independent director" as defined under the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the listing requirements and rules of The NASDAQ Stock Market. The Board has also determined that Mr. Bettinger satisfies the additional audit committee independence requirements of Rule 10A-3 and Nasdaq Listing Rule 5605(c)(2)(A) and qualifies as an "audit committee financial expert" as defined in Item 407(d)(5) of Regulation S-K. The Board has also determined that each of Ms. Morris and Mr. Goodarzi satisfies the additional independence requirements applicable to members of the Executive Compensation Committee under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5605(d)(2)(A) and Rule 10C-1 under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, and qualifies as a “non-employee director” within the meaning of Rule 16b-3 thereunder. Donna C. Morris, age 59, is the Executive Vice President and Chief People Officer of Walmart Inc., a technology-powered omnichannel retailer, a position she has held since February 2020, where she is a member of Walmart's executive committee and leads the company's global people strategy. From April 2002 to January 2020, Ms. Morris held various roles at Adobe Inc., including most recently Chief Human Resources Officer and Executive Vice President, Employee Experience. Ms. Morris previously served as a director of Marvell Technology Group Ltd., the Company's predecessor, from May 2018 until July 2020. She currently serves on the boards of directors of UKG Inc., PhonePe and the Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art, and is a trustee of Fordham University. Ms. Morris holds a bachelor's degree in political science from Carleton University and is a Fellow of the National Academy of Human Resources. Douglas R. Bettinger, age 59, is the Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Lam Research Corporation, a semiconductor equipment company, with responsibility for Finance, Tax, Treasury, Investor Relations and Corporate Analytics, and has served at Lam Research since 2013. Prior to joining Lam Research, Mr. Bettinger served as Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Avago Technologies (now Broadcom Inc.) from 2008 to 2013. From 2007 to 2008, he served as Vice President of Finance and Corporate Controller at Xilinx, Inc., and from 2004 to 2007, he was Chief Financial Officer at 24/7 Customer. Mr. Bettinger worked at Intel Corporation from 1993 to 2004, where he held several senior-level finance positions. Mr. Bettinger currently serves on the board of directors of Lattice Semiconductor Corporation and the Industrial Advisory Board of the University of Wisconsin College of Engineering, and from 2018 to 2025 served on the SEMI Board of Industry Leaders. Mr. Bettinger earned an M.B.A. in finance from the University of Michigan and a B.S. in economics from the University of Wisconsin–Madison. Sasan K. Goodarzi, age 58, has served as President and Chief Executive Officer and a member of the board of directors of Intuit Inc., a global financial technology platform company, since January 2019, and as Chairman of its board of directors since January 2026. He previously served as Executive Vice President and General Manager of Intuit's Small Business Group from 2016 to 2018, Executive Vice President and General Manager of Intuit's Consumer Tax Group from 2015 to 2016, Senior Vice President and General Manager of the Consumer Tax Group from 2013 to 2015, and Senior Vice President and Chief Information Officer from 2011 to 2013, having rejoined Intuit after serving as Chief Executive Officer of Nexant Inc. beginning in November 2010. During his previous tenure at Intuit from 2004 to 2010, Mr. Goodarzi led several business units. Prior to Intuit, he served as Global President of the Products group at Invensys and held senior leadership roles at Honeywell Inc. From April 2018 to January 2026, Mr. Goodarzi served on the board of directors of Atlassian Corporation. He holds a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from the University of Central Florida and an M.B.A. from the Kellogg School of Management at Northwestern University. There are no family relationships between any of Ms. Morris, Mr. Bettinger or Mr. Goodarzi and any other director or executive officer of the Company. There are no transactions between any of Ms. Morris, Mr. Bettinger or Mr. Goodarzi, or any member of their immediate families, and the Company that would be reportable under Item 404(a) of Regulation S-K. Further, there is no arrangement or understanding between any of Ms. Morris, Mr. Bettinger or Mr. Goodarzi and any other persons or entities pursuant to which he or she was appointed as a director of the Company. Each of Ms. Morris, Mr. Bettinger and Mr. Goodarzi will participate in all director compensation and benefit programs in which the Company's other non-employee directors participate, including an annual director retainer of $100,000 and an annual equity grant of restricted stock units valued at $250,000. In addition, each of Ms. Morris and Mr. Goodarzi will receive an annual Executive Compensation Committee member fee of $10,000 and Mr. Bettinger will receive an annual Audit Committee member fee of $15,000. Upon joining the Board, each of them received a restricted stock unit award valued in an amount equal to a prorated portion of the annual equity grant, which prorated grant will vest on the date of the 2027 annual meeting of stockholders. The Company also expects to enter into its standard form of indemnification agreement with each of Ms. Morris, Mr. Bettinger and Mr. Goodarzi, the form of which was filed as Exhibit 10.1 to the Company's Form 8-K filed on April 20, 2021 and is incorporated herein by reference. A copy of the press release announcing these appointments is furnished herewith as Exhibit 99.1 to this Current Report on Form 8-K. Item 9.01 Financial Statements and Exhibits. (d) Exhibits. Mr. Bettinger worked at Intel Corporation from 1993 to 2004, where he held several senior-level finance positions. Mr. Bettinger currently serves on the board of directors of Lattice Semiconductor Corporation and the Industrial Advisory Board of the University of Wisconsin College of Engineering, and from 2018 to 2025 served on the SEMI Board of Industry Leaders. Mr. Bettinger earned an M.B.A. in finance from the University of Michigan and a B.S. in economics from the University of Wisconsin–Madison.

Sasan K. Goodarzi, age 58, has served as President and Chief Executive Officer and a member of the board of directors of Intuit Inc., a global financial technology platform company, since January 2019, and as Chairman of its board of directors since January 2026. He previously served as Executive Vice President and General Manager of Intuit's Small Business Group from 2016 to 2018, Executive Vice President and General Manager of Intuit's Consumer Tax Group from 2015 to 2016, Senior Vice President and General Manager of the Consumer Tax Group from 2013 to 2015, and Senior Vice President and Chief Information Officer from 2011 to 2013, having rejoined Intuit after serving as Chief Executive Officer of Nexant Inc. beginning in November 2010. During his previous tenure at Intuit from 2004 to 2010, Mr. Goodarzi led several business units. Prior to Intuit, he served as Global President of the Products group at Invensys and held senior leadership roles at Honeywell Inc. From April 2018 to January 2026, Mr. Goodarzi served on the board of directors of Atlassian Corporation. He holds a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from the University of Central Florida and an M.B.A. from the Kellogg School of Management at Northwestern University.

There are no family relationships between any of Ms. Morris, Mr. Bettinger or Mr. Goodarzi and any other director or executive officer of the Company. There are no transactions between any of Ms. Morris, Mr. Bettinger or Mr. Goodarzi, or any member of their immediate families, and the Company that would be reportable under Item 404(a) of Regulation S-K. Further, there is no arrangement or understanding between any of Ms. Morris, Mr. Bettinger or Mr. Goodarzi and any other persons or entities pursuant to which he or she was appointed as a director of the Company.

Each of Ms. Morris, Mr. Bettinger and Mr. Goodarzi will participate in all director compensation and benefit programs in which the Company's other non-employee directors participate, including an annual director retainer of $100,000 and an annual equity grant of restricted stock units valued at $250,000. In addition, each of Ms. Morris and Mr. Goodarzi will receive an annual Executive Compensation Committee member fee of $10,000 and Mr. Bettinger will receive an annual Audit Committee member fee of $15,000. Upon joining the Board, each of them received a restricted stock unit award valued in an amount equal to a prorated portion of the annual equity grant, which prorated grant will vest on the date of the 2027 annual meeting of stockholders. The Company also expects to enter into its standard form of indemnification agreement with each of Ms. Morris, Mr. Bettinger and Mr. Goodarzi, the form of which was filed as Exhibit 10.1 to the Company's Form 8-K filed on April 20, 2021 and is incorporated herein by reference.
A copy of the press release announcing these appointments is furnished herewith as Exhibit 99.1 to this Current Report on Form 8-K.

Entry Into a Material Definitive Agreement. The Merger On November 1, 2026, Marvell Technology, Inc., a Delaware corporation (“ Marvell ”) entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the “ Merger Agreement ”) with Lumentum Holdings Inc., a Delaware corporation (“ Lumentum ”), Java Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of Marvell (“ Merger Sub I ”) and Java Merger Sub II, Inc., a Delaware corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of Marvell (“ Merger Sub II ” and together with Merger Sub I, each a “ Merger Sub ” and collectively the “ Merger Subs ”). Upon the terms and subject to the conditions of the Merger Agreement, Merger Sub I will merge with and into Lumentum (the “ First Merger ”), with Lumentum continuing as the surviving corporation (the “ Surviving Corporation ”) and as a wholly owned subsidiary of Marvell, and promptly following the Effective Time (as defined below), the Surviving Corporation will merge with and into Merger Sub II (the “ Second Merger ” and, collectively or in seriatim with the First Merger, as applicable, the “ Merger ”), with Merger Sub II continuing as the surviving corporation of the Second Merger (the “ Second Surviving Corporation ”). The board of directors of Marvell (the “ Marvell Board ”) has unanimously: (i) approved and declared advisable the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, including the Merger, an amendment of Marvell’s Second Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation (the “ Charter ”) to increase the number of authorized shares of Marvell Common Stock thereunder (the “ Charter Amendment ”), the issuance of the shares of Marvell Common Stock and, if applicable, Marvell Series B Preferred Stock, in connection with the Merger (the “ Share Issuance ”), (ii) determined that the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereby, including the Merger, the Charter Amendment and the Share Issuance, are fair to, and in the best interests of, Marvell and its stockholders, and (iii) resolved to recommend that Marvell’s stockholders approve the Charter Amendment and the Share Issuance. Merger Consideration At the effective time of the First Merger (the “ Effective Time ”), each share of common stock, par value $0.001 per share, of Lumentum (the “ Lumentum Common Stock ”) that is issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time, subject to certain exceptions in the Merger Agreement, will be converted into the right to receive 4.500 shares of common stock, par value $0.002 per share, of Marvell (the “ Marvell Common Stock ,” and such ratio, the “ Exchange Ratio ”), with cash in lieu of fractional shares of Marvell Common Stock payable in accordance with the Merger Agreement (the “ Common Stock Merger Consideration ”). At the Effective Time, each share of preferred stock, par value $0.001 per share, of Lumentum designated as Series A Convertible Preferred Stock (the “ Lumentum Series A Preferred Stock ” and, together with the Lumentum Common Stock, the “ Lumentum Capital Stock ”) that is issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time, subject to certain exceptions in the Merger Agreement, will be converted into the right to receive a number of shares of Marvell Common Stock equal to the product of (a) the number of shares of Lumentum Common Stock into which such share of Lumentum Preferred Stock is convertible pursuant to its terms as of immediately prior to the Effective Time and (b) the Exchange Ratio, with cash in lieu of fractional shares of Marvell Common Stock payable in accordance with the Merger Agreement (the “ Preferred Common Stock Merger Consideration ”). However, if a holder of shares of Lumentum Series A Preferred Stock makes an election in accordance with the terms of the Merger Agreement to receive the Merger Consideration in the form of Series B Convertible Preferred Stock, par value $0.002 per share, of Marvell (the “ Marvell Series B Preferred Stock ,” and such election, a “ Preferred Stock Election ”), then each share of Lumentum Preferred Stock that is held by such holder immediately prior to the Effective Time will instead be converted into the right to receive one share of Marvell Series B Preferred Stock (the “ Series B Preferred Stock Merger Consideration ” and together with the Preferred Common Stock Merger Consideration and the Common Stock Merger Consideration, the “ Merger Consideration ”). The Marvell Series B Preferred Stock is intended to have the same terms and rights as the Lumentum Series A Preferred Stock, except that each share is convertible for the Preferred Common Stock Merger Consideration. The shares of Marvell Common Stock to be issued in connection with the Merger will be listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market (“ Nasdaq ”). In connection with the issuance of the Merger Consideration by Marvell, as promptly as reasonably practicable following the date of the Merger Agreement, Marvell and Lumentum will jointly prepare and cause to be filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “ SEC ”) a registration statement on Form S-4 (the “ Form S-4 ”), which will include the joint proxy statement of Marvell and Lumentum for their respective meetings of stockholders relating to the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement. Treatment of Equity Awards Under the terms of the Merger Agreement, each Lumentum equity award, consisting of stock options, restricted stock units and performance stock units, that is outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time will be converted into an equivalent Marvell equity award, including with respect to vesting conditions (including termination protection and provisions, expiration and post-termination exercisability), except that performance stock units will be converted into solely time-vesting restricted stock units. The number of shares of Marvell Common Stock subject to each converted equity award will be equal to the number of shares of Lumentum Common Stock then subject to the award (with the number of shares subject to any performance stock unit determined based on (i) the greater of target and actual performance levels for stock price performance metrics and (ii) except as otherwise provided by the terms of Lumentum’s Change in Control and Severance Benefits Plan, as amended and restated, that would apply assuming a participant’s qualifying termination of employment upon the consummation of the Merger, at projected actual performance for all other performance metrics measured through the Effective Time), multiplied by the Exchange Ratio, and the exercise price of each converted stock option will be equal to the exercise price of the Lumentum stock option divided by the Exchange Ratio. Notwithstanding the foregoing, each restricted stock unit of Lumentum that is outstanding and held by a non-employee director as of immediately prior to the Effective Time will instead be cancelled and converted into the right to receive the Common Stock Merger Consideration. Post-Closing Governance Effective as of immediately following the Effective Time, Marvell will appoint three (3) individuals designated by Lumentum from among the members of the Lumentum board of directors and reasonably acceptable to Marvell to the Marvell Board, and Marvell will nominate each such designee who is still serving for election at Marvell’s first annual meeting of stockholders following the Effective Time. Representations, Warranties and Covenants The Merger Agreement contains customary representations and warranties of Marvell and Lumentum relating to their respective businesses. Additionally, the Merger Agreement provides for customary pre-closing covenants of each of Marvell and Lumentum, including (a) subject to certain exceptions, to conduct their respective businesses in the ordinary course; (b) to cooperate and use reasonable best efforts to obtain required regulatory approvals; (c) unless the Merger Agreement is terminated in accordance with its terms, to hold a meeting of their respective stockholders to seek the requisite stockholder approvals; (d) not to solicit proposals relating to certain alternative transactions from third parties, including alternative acquisitions or business combination transactions involving Marvell or Lumentum, as applicable (an “ Alternative Transaction ”); (e) subject to certain limited exceptions, not to participate in any discussions with third parties concerning or provide nonpublic information to third parties in connection with an Alternative Transaction; and (f) subject to certain limited exceptions, not to enter into any agreement relating to an Alternative Transaction. Closing Conditions The completion of the Merger is subject to customary conditions, including, among others, (a) adoption of the Merger Agreement by Lumentum’s stockholders; (b) approval of the Share Issuance and the Charter Amendment by Marvell’s stockholders; (c) the expiration or termination of any waiting period applicable to the Merger under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended (the “ HSR Act ”), and the receipt of certain other required regulatory approvals; (d) the absence of a legal restraint imposed by certain governmental authorities; (e) effectiveness of the Form S-4; (f) authorization for listing of the shares of Marvell Common Stock to be issued in the Merger on Nasdaq; (g) the representations and warranties of Marvell and Lumentum being true and correct (subject to certain qualifications); (h) the filing of the Charter Amendment and, if a holder of Lumentum Series A Preferred Stock has made a Preferred Stock Election, the certificate of designation for the Marvell Series B Preferred Stock with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware; (i) the absence of a material adverse effect on Marvell or Lumentum; and (j) the performance in all material respects by the parties of their respective obligations under the Merger Agreement. Termination Rights The Merger Agreement contains certain customary termination rights for Marvell and Lumentum, including, among others, (a) if the Merger is not consummated by 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time on November 1, 2027, which may be extended to February 1, 2028, May 1, 2028 and August 1, 2028, in each case under certain circumstances if required regulatory approvals have not been obtained (the “ Outside Date ”); (b) if the requisite approval of Lumentum’s stockholders is not obtained at Lumentum’s stockholder meeting or if the requisite approvals of Marvell’s stockholders is not obtained at Marvell’s stockholder meeting; (c) if the other party’s board of directors withdraws its recommendation to such other party’s stockholders regarding the Merger Agreement; (d) if the other party breaches any of its representations, warranties, covenants or other agreements in a manner that would cause certain conditions to the consummation of the Merger set forth in the Merger Agreement to not be satisfied (subject to certain cure rights); (e) in certain limited circumstances, by a party in order to enter into a definitive agreement providing for unsolicited “Superior Proposal” (as defined in the Merger Agreement), on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement, including the payment by such party of the applicable Termination Fee; and (f) if any governmental entity of certain competent jurisdictions has issued a legal restraint that would cause the relevant closing condition to not be satisfied and such legal restraint has become final and non-appealable. Termination Fees If the Merger Agreement is terminated by Lumentum because the Marvell Board withdraws its recommendation to its stockholders regarding the Merger Agreement, or if Marvell terminates the Agreement to enter into a definitive agreement providing for a Superior Proposal, Marvell will be required to pay Lumentum a termination fee equal to $5.8 billion (the “ Marvell Termination Fee ”). Marvell is also required to pay the Marvell Termination Fee to Lumentum if the Merger Agreement is terminated in certain circumstances after a proposal for an Alternative Transaction is made and, within twelve months of termination, Marvell enters into a definitive agreement regarding, or consummates, an Alternative Transaction for a majority of Marvell. Lumentum is subject to reciprocal obligations to pay a termination fee equal to $2.9 billion (the “ Lumentum Termination Fee ” and, each of the Marvell Termination Fee and the Lumentum Termination Fee, a “ Termination Fee ”) to Marvell in corresponding circumstances. Marvell will be required to pay a termination fee equal to $3.2 billion to Lumentum (the “ Regulatory Termination Fee ”) if the Merger Agreement is terminated in certain circumstances related to (a) the failure to consummate the Merger prior to the Outside Date; (b) the issuance of a final and non-appealable legal restraint under the HSR Act or certain other specified antitrust or foreign investment laws; or (c) because a required regulatory approval has been denied and the denial has become final and non-appealable, if, in each case of (a)–(c), at the time of termination, all conditions to closing other than those relating to regulatory approvals and regulatory legal restraints have been satisfied (or, for those conditions to be satisfied at closing, are capable of being satisfied). The foregoing description of the Merger Agreement does not purport to be complete and is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the Merger Agreement, which is attached hereto as Exhibit 2.1 and is incorporated herein by reference. The representations, warranties and covenants of each party set forth in the Merger Agreement have been made only for the purposes of, and were and are solely for the benefit of the parties to, the Merger Agreement, may be subject to limitations agreed upon by the contracting parties, including being qualified by confidential disclosures made for the purposes of allocating contractual risk between the parties to the Merger Agreement instead of establishing these matters as facts, and may be subject to standards of materiality applicable to the contracting parties that differ from those applicable to investors. Accordingly, the representations and warranties may not describe the actual state of affairs at the date they were made or at any other time, and investors should not rely on them as statements of fact. In addition, such representations and warranties (1) will not survive consummation of the Merger, (2) were made only as of the date of the Merger Agreement or such other date as is specified in the Merger Agreement and (3) are subject to limitations agreed upon by the parties, including being qualified by confidential disclosures made by each contracting party to the other for the purposes of allocating contractual risk between them. Moreover, information concerning the subject matter of the representations and warranties may change after the date of the Merger Agreement, which subsequent information may or may not be fully reflected in the parties’ public disclosures. Accordingly, the Merger Agreement is included with this filing only to provide investors with information regarding the terms of the Merger Agreement, and not to provide investors with any factual information regarding Marvell or Lumentum, their respective affiliates or their respective businesses. The Merger Agreement should not be read alone, but should instead be read in conjunction with the other information regarding Marvell, Lumentum, their respective affiliates or their respective businesses, the Merger Agreement and the Merger that will be contained in, or incorporated by reference into, the Registration Statement on Form S-4 that will include a joint proxy statement of Marvell and Lumentum and a prospectus of Marvell, as well as in the Forms 10-K, Forms 10-Q and other filings that each of Marvell and Lumentum make with the SEC. Additional Information About the Transaction and Where to Find It This communication relates to a proposed transaction between Marvell and Lumentum (the “Transaction”). In connection with the Transaction, Marvell intends to file with the SEC a registration statement on Form S-4 (the “Form S-4”) that will include a joint proxy statement for Marvell’s and Lumentum’s respective stockholders and that will also constitute a prospectus with respect to the shares of Marvell’s common stock to be issued in the Transaction (the “Joint Proxy Statement/Prospectus”). The definitive Joint Proxy Statement/Prospectus (if and when available) will be mailed to stockholders of Marvell and Lumentum after the Form S-4 is declared effective by the SEC. This communication is not a substitute for the Joint Proxy Statement/Prospectus or registration statement. Investors and security holders will be able to obtain free copies of the Form S-4 and Joint Proxy Statement/Prospectus and other documents containing important information about Marvell, Lumentum and the Transaction, once such documents are filed with the SEC through the website maintained by the SEC at https://www.sec.gov . Copies of the documents filed with the SEC by Marvell will be available online free of charge on Marvell’s website at https://investor.marvell.com or by contacting Marvell’s Investor Relations department at ir@marvell.com . Copies of the documents filed with the SEC by Lumentum will be available online free of charge on Lumentum’s website at https://investor.lumentum.com or by contacting Lumentum’s Investor Relations department at investor.relations@lumentum.com . Item 1.01.

Entry Into a Material Definitive Agreement.

The Merger

On November 1, 2026, Marvell Technology, Inc., a Delaware corporation (“Marvell”) entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the “Merger Agreement”) with Lumentum Holdings Inc., a Delaware corporation (“Lumentum”), Java Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of Marvell (“Merger Sub I”) and Java Merger Sub II, Inc., a Delaware corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of Marvell (“Merger Sub II” and together with Merger Sub I, each a “Merger Sub” and collectively the “Merger Subs”).

Upon the terms and subject to the conditions of the Merger Agreement, Merger Sub I will merge with and into Lumentum (the “First Merger”), with Lumentum continuing as the surviving corporation (the “Surviving Corporation”) and as a wholly owned subsidiary of Marvell, and promptly following the Effective Time (as defined below), the Surviving Corporation will merge with and into Merger Sub II (the “Second Merger” and, collectively or in seriatim with the First Merger, as applicable, the “Merger”), with Merger Sub II continuing as the surviving corporation of the Second Merger (the “Second Surviving Corporation”).

The board of directors of Marvell (the “Marvell Board”) has unanimously: (i) approved and declared advisable the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, including the Merger, an amendment of Marvell’s Second Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation (the “Charter”) to increase the number of authorized shares of Marvell Common Stock thereunder (the “Charter Amendment”), the issuance of the shares of Marvell Common Stock and, if applicable, Marvell Series B Preferred Stock, in connection with the Merger (the “Share Issuance”), (ii) determined that the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereby, including the Merger, the Charter Amendment and the Share Issuance, are fair to, and in the best interests of, Marvell and its stockholders, and (iii) resolved to recommend that Marvell’s stockholders approve the Charter Amendment and the Share Issuance.

Merger Consideration

At the effective time of the First Merger (the “Effective Time”), each share of common stock, par value $0.001 per share, of Lumentum (the “Lumentum Common Stock”) that is issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time, subject to certain exceptions in the Merger Agreement, will be converted into the right to receive 4.500 shares of common stock, par value $0.002 per share, of Marvell (the “Marvell Common Stock,” and such ratio, the “Exchange Ratio”), with cash in lieu of fractional shares of Marvell Common Stock payable in accordance with the Merger Agreement (the “Common Stock Merger Consideration”).

At the Effective Time, each share of preferred stock, par value $0.001 per share, of Lumentum designated as Series A Convertible Preferred Stock (the “Lumentum Series A Preferred Stock” and, together with the Lumentum Common Stock, the “Lumentum Capital Stock”) that is issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time, subject to certain exceptions in the Merger Agreement, will be converted into the right to receive a number of shares of Marvell Common Stock equal to the product of (a) the number of shares of Lumentum Common Stock into which such share of Lumentum Preferred Stock is convertible pursuant to its terms as of immediately prior to the Effective Time and (b) the Exchange Ratio, with cash in lieu of fractional shares of Marvell Common Stock payable in accordance with the Merger Agreement (the “Preferred Common Stock Merger Consideration”).

However, if a holder of shares of Lumentum Series A Preferred Stock makes an election in accordance with the terms of the Merger Agreement to receive the Merger Consideration in the form of Series B Convertible Preferred Stock, par value $0.002 per share, of Marvell (the “Marvell Series B Preferred Stock,” and such election, a “Preferred Stock Election”), then each share of Lumentum Preferred Stock that is held by such holder immediately prior to the Effective Time will instead be converted into the right to receive one share of Marvell Series B Preferred Stock (the “Series B Preferred Stock Merger Consideration” and together with the Preferred Common Stock Merger Consideration and the Common Stock Merger Consideration, the “Merger Consideration”). The Marvell Series B Preferred Stock is intended to have the same terms and rights as the Lumentum Series A Preferred Stock, except that each share is convertible for the Preferred Common Stock Merger Consideration.

 

The shares of Marvell Common Stock to be issued in connection with the Merger will be listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market (“Nasdaq”). In connection with the issuance of the Merger Consideration by Marvell, as promptly as reasonably practicable following the date of the Merger Agreement, Marvell and Lumentum will jointly prepare and cause to be filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) a registration statement on Form S-4 (the “Form S-4”), which will include the joint proxy statement of Marvell and Lumentum for their respective meetings of stockholders relating to the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement.

Treatment of Equity Awards

Under the terms of the Merger Agreement, each Lumentum equity award, consisting of stock options, restricted stock units and performance stock units, that is outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time will be converted into an equivalent Marvell equity award, including with respect to vesting conditions (including termination protection and provisions, expiration and post-termination exercisability), except that performance stock units will be converted into solely time-vesting restricted stock units. The number of shares of Marvell Common Stock subject to each converted equity award will be equal to the number of shares of Lumentum Common Stock then subject to the award (with the number of shares subject to any performance stock unit determined based on (i) the greater of target and actual performance levels for stock price performance metrics and (ii) except as otherwise provided by the terms of Lumentum’s Change in Control and Severance Benefits Plan, as amended and restated, that would apply assuming a participant’s qualifying termination of employment upon the consummation of the Merger, at projected actual performance for all other performance metrics measured through the Effective Time), multiplied by the Exchange Ratio, and the exercise price of each converted stock option will be equal to the exercise price of the Lumentum stock option divided by the Exchange Ratio.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, each restricted stock unit of Lumentum that is outstanding and held by a non-employee director as of immediately prior to the Effective Time will instead be cancelled and converted into the right to receive the Common Stock Merger Consideration.

Post-Closing Governance

Effective as of immediately following the Effective Time, Marvell will appoint three (3) individuals designated by Lumentum from among the members of the Lumentum board of directors and reasonably acceptable to Marvell to the Marvell Board, and Marvell will nominate each such designee who is still serving for election at Marvell’s first annual meeting of stockholders following the Effective Time.

Representations, Warranties and Covenants

The Merger Agreement contains customary representations and warranties of Marvell and Lumentum relating to their respective businesses. Additionally, the Merger Agreement provides for customary pre-closing covenants of each of Marvell and Lumentum, including (a) subject to certain exceptions, to conduct their respective businesses in the ordinary course; (b) to cooperate and use reasonable best efforts to obtain required regulatory approvals; (c) unless the Merger Agreement is terminated in accordance with its terms, to hold a meeting of their respective stockholders to seek the requisite stockholder approvals; (d) not to solicit proposals relating to certain alternative transactions from third parties, including alternative acquisitions or business combination transactions involving Marvell or Lumentum, as applicable (an “Alternative Transaction”); (e) subject to certain limited exceptions, not to participate in any discussions with third parties concerning or provide nonpublic information to third parties in connection with an Alternative Transaction; and (f) subject to certain limited exceptions, not to enter into any agreement relating to an Alternative Transaction.

Closing Conditions

The completion of the Merger is subject to customary conditions, including, among others, (a) adoption of the Merger Agreement by Lumentum’s stockholders; (b) approval of the Share Issuance and the Charter Amendment by Marvell’s stockholders; (c) the expiration or termination of any waiting period applicable to the Merger under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended (the “HSR Act”), and the receipt of certain other required regulatory approvals; (d) the absence of a legal restraint imposed by certain governmental authorities; (e) effectiveness of the Form S-4; (f) authorization for listing of the shares of Marvell Common Stock to be issued in

the Merger on Nasdaq; (g) the representations and warranties of Marvell and Lumentum being true and correct (subject to certain qualifications); (h) the filing of the Charter Amendment and, if a holder of Lumentum Series A Preferred Stock has made a Preferred Stock Election, the certificate of designation for the Marvell Series B Preferred Stock with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware; (i) the absence of a material adverse effect on Marvell or Lumentum; and (j) the performance in all material respects by the parties of their respective obligations under the Merger Agreement.

Termination Rights

The Merger Agreement contains certain customary termination rights for Marvell and Lumentum, including, among others, (a) if the Merger is not consummated by 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time on November 1, 2027, which may be extended to February 1, 2028, May 1, 2028 and August 1, 2028, in each case under certain circumstances if required regulatory approvals have not been obtained (the “Outside Date”); (b) if the requisite approval of Lumentum’s stockholders is not obtained at Lumentum’s stockholder meeting or if the requisite approvals of Marvell’s stockholders is not obtained at Marvell’s stockholder meeting; (c) if the other party’s board of directors withdraws its recommendation to such other party’s stockholders regarding the Merger Agreement; (d) if the other party breaches any of its representations, warranties, covenants or other agreements in a manner that would cause certain conditions to the consummation of the Merger set forth in the Merger Agreement to not be satisfied (subject to certain cure rights); (e) in certain limited circumstances, by a party in order to enter into a definitive agreement providing for unsolicited “Superior Proposal” (as defined in the Merger Agreement), on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement, including the payment by such party of the applicable Termination Fee; and (f) if any governmental entity of certain competent jurisdictions has issued a legal restraint that would cause the relevant closing condition to not be satisfied and such legal restraint has become final and non-appealable.

Termination Fees

If the Merger Agreement is terminated by Lumentum because the Marvell Board withdraws its recommendation to its stockholders regarding the Merger Agreement, or if Marvell terminates the Agreement to enter into a definitive agreement providing for a Superior Proposal, Marvell will be required to pay Lumentum a termination fee equal to $5.8 billion (the “Marvell Termination Fee”). Marvell is also required to pay the Marvell Termination Fee to Lumentum if the Merger Agreement is terminated in certain circumstances after a proposal for an Alternative Transaction is made and, within twelve months of termination, Marvell enters into a definitive agreement regarding, or consummates, an Alternative Transaction for a majority of Marvell. Lumentum is subject to reciprocal obligations to pay a termination fee equal to $2.9 billion (the “Lumentum Termination Fee” and, each of the Marvell Termination Fee and the Lumentum Termination Fee, a “Termination Fee”) to Marvell in corresponding circumstances.

Marvell will be required to pay a termination fee equal to $3.2 billion to Lumentum (the “Regulatory Termination Fee”) if the Merger Agreement is terminated in certain circumstances related to (a) the failure to consummate the Merger prior to the Outside Date; (b) the issuance of a final and non-appealable legal restraint under the HSR Act or certain other specified antitrust or foreign investment laws; or (c) because a required regulatory approval has been denied and the denial has become final and non-appealable, if, in each case of (a)–(c), at the time of termination, all conditions to closing other than those relating to regulatory approvals and regulatory legal restraints have been satisfied (or, for those conditions to be satisfied at closing, are capable of being satisfied).

text: Exhibit 99.1 MARVELL AND LUMENTUM TO COMBINE, CREATING A CATEGORY LEADER IN AI CONNECTIVITY • Combines two of the fastest-growing enablers of AI, bringing together complementary electrical and optical technologies to address increasingly complex connectivity requirements across next-generation AI infrastructure • Expected to create a broad full-stack connectivity portfolio that is intended to enable end-to-end extreme co-design, high-volume production of fully-optimized, pre-validated optical solutions and faster time to market for customers • Expected to expand the combined company’s total addressable market to $550 billion • The transaction is expected to enhance the combined company’s long-term revenue growth, non-GAAP gross margin and non-GAAP operating margin profile, provide line of sight to more than $1 billion in annual run-rate cost synergies, and is expected to be accretive to Marvell non-GAAP earnings per share in year one post-close SANTA CLARA, Calif. and SAN JOSE, Calif. – November 2, 2026 – Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL) and Lumentum (NASDAQ: LITE) today announced that they have entered into a definitive agreement for Marvell to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction. Under the terms of the agreement, Lumentum stockholders will receive a fixed exchange ratio of 4.500 shares of Marvell common stock for each share of Lumentum common stock they own. The transaction has an implied enterprise value of $115 billion for Lumentum, representing approximately $1,132 per share of Lumentum common stock and a premium of approximately 23.9% based on each company’s unaffected closing share price as of October 28, 2026, the last trading day before market speculation regarding a potential transaction began. Post-closing, current Marvell stockholders will own approximately 67% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis, while Lumentum stockholders will own approximately 33%. The AI infrastructure industry is at an inflection point. Rapidly growing bandwidth requirements and the physical limitations of copper-based connectivity are accelerating the transition toward optical technologies. As AI infrastructure scales to increasingly complex architectures, particularly scale-up and scale-in, the industry is shifting from discrete, modular components toward highly integrated optical solutions that require much closer co-design of electrical and optical technologies to deliver greater bandwidth, performance and energy efficiency. The combination brings together best-in-breed technology to meet this need, joining Marvell’s strengths in electrical and optical interconnect, network switching, custom XPU and XPU attach, and advanced semiconductor technologies with Lumentum’s expertise in high-performance lasers, optical transceivers, optical circuit switching (OCS) and specialized compound semiconductor manufacturing. Following closing, the combined company is expected to offer a highly complementary portfolio spanning leading-edge CMOS, silicon photonics, compound semiconductors, advanced packaging and manufacturing capabilities. The combination is intended to enable deeper integration and co-design across the electrical and optical signal chain, positioning Marvell to deliver highly optimized connectivity solutions across a wide range of distances, from distributed data centers to connections within advanced semiconductor packages. “AI infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental architectural shift toward optical connectivity, creating an opportunity that comes along once in a generation,” said Matt Murphy, Chairman and CEO of Marvell. “The companies that move first and help define this transition will set the standard for decades to come. By bringing together two leaders with highly complementary technologies, exceptional talent and specialized manufacturing capabilities, we intend to help shape the next era of AI connectivity and create exceptional stockholder value.” “Joining Marvell creates a company uniquely positioned to capitalize on a market opportunity of $550 billion and generate significant, sustainable stockholder value,” said Michael Hurlston, President and CEO of Lumentum. “Surging AI data traffic requires rapid hardware innovation, and this combination enhances our ability to deliver next-generation solutions at scale. Together with Marvell, we will meet our customers’ complete interconnect needs, spanning scale-across and scale-out today to scale-up and scale-in domains tomorrow. By offering extreme co-design around our customers’ demanding requirements, we will help them achieve faster time to market, accelerated innovation cycles, and category-defining performance.” Compelling Strategic and Financial Rationale The combination is expected to deliver substantial strategic and financial benefits: • Creates a category leader in AI connectivity: Combining Marvell’s electrical and optical interconnect, switching and custom silicon technologies with Lumentum’s high-performance lasers, optical transceivers and OCS capabilities will create a comprehensive connectivity portfolio spanning scale-across, scale-out, scale-up and scale-in. Upon closing, the combined company anticipates being positioned to address customer connectivity requirements across a broad range of distances and topologies, from distributed data centers to advanced semiconductor packages. • Enables end-to-end extreme co-design and accelerates customer innovation: As AI infrastructure becomes increasingly complex, customers require higher levels of integration and optimization across digital, analog and optical technologies. By bringing together complementary technologies and engineering expertise across the signal chain, the combined company expects to be positioned to develop highly-optimized, pre-validated optical solutions designed to improve bandwidth, performance and power efficiency, accelerate customer time to market and support high-volume production. • Combines highly specialized manufacturing capabilities and enhances R&D resources: Lumentum brings advanced compound semiconductor manufacturing and process technologies, including indium phosphide (InP), as well as high-speed and high-power laser capabilities. After closing, the combined company plans to bring together leading-edge semiconductor design, advanced packaging and specialized manufacturing capabilities to enable deeper heterogeneous integration, strengthen strategic supply and accelerate the development of next-generation optical technologies. • Creates significant long-term stockholder value: The combination brings together two of the fastest-growing companies enabling AI infrastructure and expands the combined company’s total addressable market to $550 billion and enhances the combined company’s ability to serve customers in emerging scale-up and scale-in markets. The transaction is expected to enhance the combined company’s long-term revenue growth, non-GAAP gross margin and non-GAAP operating margin profile, provide line of sight to more than $1 billion in annual run-rate cost synergies, and is expected to be accretive to Marvell non-GAAP earnings per share in year one post-close. Transaction Structure and Terms Under the terms of the agreement, which has been unanimously approved by the boards of directors of both companies, Lumentum stockholders will receive a fixed exchange ratio of 4.500 shares of Marvell common stock for each share of Lumentum common stock held at the time of closing, implying pro forma ownership of approximately 33% of the combined company for Lumentum stockholders on a fully diluted basis. Following closing, Matt Murphy will continue as Chairman and CEO of the combined company. As part of the transaction, three members of Lumentum’s Board of Directors, including Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston, will join Marvell’s Board, which currently consists of seven directors. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of calendar year 2028, subject to approval by Marvell and Lumentum stockholders, receipt of regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions. Marvell Reports Preliminary Revenue for the Fiscal Third Quarter 2027 and Lumentum Issues Fiscal First Quarter 2027 Results In connection with today’s announcement, Marvell today reported preliminary revenue for the third quarter of fiscal 2027 consistent with previously provided guidance, maintaining the midpoint of its prior guidance while narrowing the expected range to plus or minus 2%, compared with the original range of plus or minus 5%. About Marvell To deliver the data infrastructure technology that connects the world, we’re building solutions on the most powerful foundation: our partnerships with our customers. Trusted by the world’s leading technology companies for over 30 years, we move, store, process and secure the world’s data with semiconductor solutions designed for our customers’ current needs and future ambitions. Through a process of deep collaboration and transparency, we’re ultimately changing the way tomorrow’s enterprise, cloud and carrier architectures transform—for the better. About Lumentum Lumentum is a global leader in optical and photonic technologies that power the networks and infrastructure behind AI, cloud computing, and next-generation communications. Built on decades of photonics innovation, Lumentum delivers high-performance lasers, modules, and optical subsystems that enable scalable, energy-efficient data center connectivity, advanced telecom networks, industrial manufacturing, and sensing applications. Headquartered in San Jose, California, the company operates R&D, manufacturing, and sales facilities worldwide. Learn more at www.lumentum.com. As AI infrastructure scales to increasingly complex architectures, particularly scale-up and scale-in, the industry is shifting from discrete, modular components toward highly integrated optical solutions that require much closer co-design of electrical and optical technologies to deliver greater bandwidth, performance and energy efficiency.

The combination brings together best-in-breed technology to meet this need, joining Marvell’s strengths in electrical and optical interconnect, network switching, custom XPU and XPU attach, and advanced semiconductor technologies with Lumentum’s expertise in high-performance lasers, optical transceivers, optical circuit switching (OCS) and specialized compound semiconductor manufacturing. Following closing, the combined company is expected to offer a highly complementary portfolio spanning leading-edge CMOS, silicon photonics, compound semiconductors, advanced packaging and manufacturing capabilities. The combination is intended to enable deeper integration and co-design across the electrical and optical signal chain, positioning Marvell to deliver highly optimized connectivity solutions across a wide range of distances, from distributed data centers to connections within advanced semiconductor packages.

“AI infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental architectural shift toward optical connectivity, creating an opportunity that comes along once in a generation,” said Matt Murphy, Chairman and CEO of Marvell. “The companies that move first and help define this transition will set the standard for decades to come. By bringing together two leaders with highly complementary technologies, exceptional talent and specialized manufacturing capabilities, we intend to help shape the next era of AI connectivity and create exceptional stockholder value.”

“Joining Marvell creates a company uniquely positioned to capitalize on a market opportunity of $550 billion and generate significant, sustainable stockholder value,” said Michael Hurlston, President and CEO of Lumentum. “Surging AI data traffic requires rapid hardware innovation, and this combination enhances our ability to deliver next-generation solutions at scale. Together with Marvell, we will meet our customers’ complete interconnect needs, spanning scale-across and scale-out today to scale-up and scale-in domains tomorrow. By offering extreme co-design around our customers’ demanding requirements, we will help them achieve faster time to market, accelerated innovation cycles, and category-defining performance.”

Compelling Strategic and Financial Rationale

The combination is expected to deliver substantial strategic and financial benefits:

 

  •  

Creates a category leader in AI connectivity: Combining Marvell’s electrical and optical interconnect, switching and custom silicon technologies with Lumentum’s high-performance lasers, optical transceivers and OCS capabilities will create a comprehensive connectivity portfolio spanning scale-across, scale-out, scale-up and scale-in. Upon closing, the combined company anticipates being positioned to address customer connectivity requirements across a broad range of distances and topologies, from distributed data centers to advanced semiconductor packages.

 

  •  

Enables end-to-end extreme co-design and accelerates customer innovation: As AI infrastructure becomes increasingly complex, customers require higher levels of integration and optimization across digital, analog and optical technologies. By bringing together complementary technologies and engineering expertise across the signal chain, the combined company expects to be positioned to develop highly-optimized, pre-validated optical solutions designed to improve bandwidth, performance and power efficiency, accelerate customer time to market and support high-volume production.

 

  •  

Combines highly specialized manufacturing capabilities and enhances R&D resources: Lumentum brings advanced compound semiconductor manufacturing and process technologies, including indium phosphide (InP), as well as high-speed and high-power laser capabilities. After closing, the combined company plans to bring together leading-edge semiconductor design, advanced packaging and specialized manufacturing capabilities to enable deeper heterogeneous integration, strengthen strategic supply and accelerate the development of next-generation optical technologies.

 

  •  

Creates significant long-term stockholder value: The combination brings together two of the fastest-growing companies enabling AI infrastructure and expands the combined company’s total addressable market to $550 billion and enhances the combined company’s ability to serve customers in emerging scale-up and scale-in markets. The transaction is expected to enhance the combined company’s long-term revenue growth, non-GAAP gross margin and non-GAAP operating margin profile, provide line of sight to more than $1 billion in annual run-rate cost synergies, and is expected to be accretive to Marvell non-GAAP earnings per share in year one post-close.

Transaction Structure and Terms

Under the terms of the agreement, which has been unanimously approved by the boards of directors of both companies, Lumentum stockholders will receive a fixed exchange ratio of 4.500 shares of Marvell common stock for each share of Lumentum common stock held at the time of closing, implying pro forma ownership of approximately 33% of the combined company for Lumentum stockholders on a fully diluted basis.

Following closing, Matt Murphy will continue as Chairman and CEO of the combined company. As part of the transaction, three members of Lumentum’s Board of Directors, including Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston, will join Marvell’s Board, which currently consists of seven directors.

The transaction is expected to close in the first half of calendar year 2028, subject to approval by Marvell and Lumentum stockholders, receipt of regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions.

Marvell Reports Preliminary Revenue for the Fiscal Third Quarter 2027 and Lumentum Issues Fiscal First Quarter 2027 Results

In connection with today’s announcement, Marvell today reported preliminary revenue for the third quarter of fiscal 2027 consistent with previously provided guidance, maintaining the midpoint of its prior guidance while narrowing the expected range to plus or minus 2%, compared with the original range of plus or minus 5%.

Lumentum today separately reported financial results for its first fiscal quarter of 2027. Lumentum’s financial results can be found on the Investors section of the Lumentum website at http://investor.Lumentum.com.

About Marvell

To deliver the data infrastructure technology that connects the world, we’re building solutions on the most powerful foundation: our partnerships with our customers. Trusted by the world’s leading technology companies for over 30 years, we move, store, process and secure the world’s data with semiconductor solutions designed for our customers’ current needs and future ambitions. Through a process of deep collaboration and transparency, we’re ultimately changing the way tomorrow’s enterprise, cloud and carrier architectures transform—for the better.

About Lumentum

Lumentum is a global leader in optical and photonic technologies that power the networks and infrastructure behind AI, cloud computing, and next-generation communications. Built on decades of photonics innovation, Lumentum delivers high-performance lasers, modules, and optical subsystems that enable scalable, energy-efficient data center connectivity, advanced telecom networks, industrial manufacturing, and sensing applications. Headquartered in San Jose, California, the company operates R&D, manufacturing, and sales facilities worldwide. Learn more at www.lumentum.com.

text: Exhibit 99.1 Supermicro Announces First Quarter of Fiscal Year 2027 Financial Results SAN JOSE, Calif. -- November 3, 2026 -- (BUSINESS WIRE) -- Super Micro Computer, Inc. (NASDAQ: SMCI) (“Supermicro” or the “Company”), an AI, Enterprise, Storage, and 5G/Edge IT Total Solution Provider, featuring Data Center Building Block Solutions® (DCBBS), today announced unaudited financial results for its first quarter ended September 30, 2026. First Quarter Fiscal Year 2027 Highlights • Net sales of $19.9 billion versus $11.1 billion in Q4'26 and $5.0 billion in Q1'26. • Gross margin of 12.7% versus 17.5% in Q4'26 and 9.3% in Q1'26. • Net income of $1,594 million versus $1,178 million in Q4'26 and $168 million in Q1'26. • Diluted net income per common share of $1.75 versus $1.62 in Q4'26 and $0.26 in Q1'26. • Non-GAAP gross margin of 12.8% versus 9.5% in Q1'26. • Non-GAAP diluted net income per common share of $1.81 versus $0.35 in Q1'26. • Cash flow used in operations for Q1'27 of $434 million and capital expenditures and investments of $47 million. “Supermicro’s transformation into a Total AI and IT Datacenter Solution provider continues to accelerate, delivering record revenue of $19.9 billion for the first quarter fiscal 2027,” said Charles Liang, Founder, President, and CEO of Supermicro. “DCBBS is driving significant value for our customers—from gigawatt-scale datacenters down to single-container PODs—which, including our expanding software, proactive service, and networking solutions, is enhancing profitability and long-term shareholder value. Through key enterprise partnerships and expanding global production capacity, we are making AI infrastructure faster to deploy, superior up-time, and more cost-effective for our customer base.” The Non-GAAP gross margin for the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 was 12.8% with adjustments for stock-based compensation expense of $8 million. The Non-GAAP diluted net income per common share for the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 was $1.81. As of September 30, 2026, total cash and cash equivalents was $6.9 billion and total bank debt and convertible notes were $8.6 billion. Business Outlook The Company expects net sales in the range of $19.5 billion and $21.5 billion for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027 ending December 31, 2026, GAAP net income per diluted share of $1.59 to $1.83 and non-GAAP net income per diluted share of $1.66 to $1.90. The Company’s projections for GAAP and non-GAAP net income per diluted share assume a tax rate of approximately 21.2% and 21.1%, respectively, and a fully diluted share count of 753 million shares for GAAP and fully diluted share count of 769 million shares for non-GAAP. The outlook for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027 GAAP net income per diluted share includes approximately $89 million in expected stock-based compensation expense, net of related tax effects of $22 million that are excluded from non-GAAP net income per diluted share. For fiscal year 2027, the Company expects net sales in the range of $72.0 billion to $82.0 billion. Conference Call and Webcast Information Supermicro will present a live audio webcast of our conference call to review its first quarter 2027 financial results on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. ET / 2:00 p.m. PT. The webcast will be available at https://ir.supermicro.com . A replay of the webcast will be available shortly after the call at the same website and will remain accessible for one year. Forward Looking Statements and Other Disclosures Statements contained in this press release that are not historical fact may be forward looking statements within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933 and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. These forward-looking statements can be identified by the use of forward-looking terminology such as “anticipate,” “believe,” “continue,” “could,” “estimate,” “expect,” “may,” “plan,” “seek,” “should,” “will,” “would” “optimistic” or similar expressions and the negatives of those terms. Such forward looking statements may include statements regarding, among other things, guidance for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027. Such forward looking statements do not constitute guarantees of future performance and are subject to a variety of risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those anticipated, including: (i) our quarterly operating results may fluctuate, (ii) as we increasingly target larger customers and larger sales opportunities, our customer base may become more concentrated, our cost of sales may increase, our margins may be lower and our sales may become less predictable for a variety of reasons, many of which are not in our control, (iii) the average sales prices for our server solutions could decline if customers do not continue to purchase our latest generation products or additional components, and (iv) adverse economic conditions could affect our business, including, but not limited to, increased tariffs. Certain prior period amounts have been reclassified to conform to the current period presentation. Additional factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those projected or suggested in any forward-looking statements are detailed in our filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including those factors discussed under the caption “Risk Factors” in such filings, particularly in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for our fiscal year ended June 30, 2026. Financial Information Is Preliminary and May Be Subject to Change The unaudited financial information presented in this press release is preliminary. The final financial results reported for this period may also differ from the results reported in this release. The financial results presented reflect the Company's preliminary estimated unaudited financial results, based upon information available to the Company as of the date of this press release. The Company has provided preliminary estimates of financial results primarily because its financial closing procedures for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 are not yet complete. The data are not a comprehensive statement of the Company's results for such periods, and the actual results may differ materially from these preliminary estimated data. The Company's actual results remain subject to the completion of management’s and its audit committee’s review and other financial closing processes as well as the completion and preparation of its financial data for such periods. The Company's independent registered public accounting firm has not audited, reviewed, compiled or performed any procedures with respect to such preliminary data. During the course of the preparation of the Company's financial statements and related notes and the completion of the review for such periods, additional adjustments to the preliminary estimated financial information presented here may be identified, and its final results for these periods may vary from these preliminary estimates. This preliminary estimated data should not be considered a substitute for the financial statements to be prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States and to be filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission once available. About Super Micro Computer, Inc. Supermicro (NASDAQ: SMCI) is a global leader in Application-Optimized Total IT Solutions. Founded and operating in San Jose, California, Supermicro is committed to delivering first-to-market innovation for Enterprise, Cloud, AI, and 5G/Edge IT Infrastructure. We are a Total IT Solutions provider with server, AI, storage, IoT, switch systems, software, and support services. Supermicro's motherboard, power, and chassis design expertise further enables our development and production, enabling next-generation innovation from cloud to edge for our global customers. Our products are designed and manufactured in-house (in the US, Taiwan, Malaysia, and the Netherlands), leveraging global operations for scale and efficiency and optimized to improve TCO and reduce environmental impact (Green Computing). The award-winning portfolio of Server Building Block Solutions® allows customers to optimize for their exact workload and application by selecting from a broad family of systems built from our flexible and reusable building blocks that support a comprehensive set of form factors, processors, memory, GPUs, storage, networking, power, and cooling solutions (air-conditioned, free air cooling, or liquid cooling). Supermicro Announces First Quarter of Fiscal Year 2027 Financial Results

SAN JOSE, Calif. -- November 3, 2026 -- (BUSINESS WIRE) -- Super Micro Computer, Inc. (NASDAQ: SMCI) (“Supermicro” or the “Company”), an AI, Enterprise, Storage, and 5G/Edge IT Total Solution Provider, featuring Data Center Building Block Solutions® (DCBBS), today announced unaudited financial results for its first quarter ended September 30, 2026.

First Quarter Fiscal Year 2027 Highlights

•Net sales of $19.9 billion versus $11.1 billion in Q4'26 and $5.0 billion in Q1'26.

•Gross margin of 12.7% versus 17.5% in Q4'26 and 9.3% in Q1'26.

•Net income of $1,594 million versus $1,178 million in Q4'26 and $168 million in Q1'26.

•Diluted net income per common share of $1.75 versus $1.62 in Q4'26 and $0.26 in Q1'26.

•Non-GAAP gross margin of 12.8% versus 9.5% in Q1'26.

•Non-GAAP diluted net income per common share of $1.81 versus $0.35 in Q1'26.

•Cash flow used in operations for Q1'27 of $434 million and capital expenditures and investments of $47 million.

“Supermicro’s transformation into a Total AI and IT Datacenter Solution provider continues to accelerate, delivering record revenue of $19.9 billion for the first quarter fiscal 2027,” said Charles Liang, Founder, President, and CEO of Supermicro. “DCBBS is driving significant value for our customers—from gigawatt-scale datacenters down to single-container PODs—which, including our expanding software, proactive service, and networking solutions, is enhancing profitability and long-term shareholder value. Through key enterprise partnerships and expanding global production capacity, we are making AI infrastructure faster to deploy, superior up-time, and more cost-effective for our customer base.”

The Non-GAAP gross margin for the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 was 12.8% with adjustments for stock-based compensation expense of $8 million. The Non-GAAP diluted net income per common share for the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 was $1.81.

As of September 30, 2026, total cash and cash equivalents was $6.9 billion and total bank debt and convertible notes were $8.6 billion.

Business Outlook

The Company expects net sales in the range of $19.5 billion and $21.5 billion for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027 ending December 31, 2026, GAAP net income per diluted share of $1.59 to $1.83 and non-GAAP net income per diluted share of $1.66 to $1.90. The Company’s projections for GAAP and non-GAAP net income per diluted share assume a tax rate of approximately 21.2% and 21.1%, respectively, and a fully diluted share count of 753 million shares for GAAP and fully diluted share count of 769 million shares for non-GAAP. The outlook for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027 GAAP net income per diluted share includes approximately $89 million in expected stock-based compensation expense, net of related tax effects of $22 million that are excluded from non-GAAP net income per diluted share.



For fiscal year 2027, the Company expects net sales in the range of $72.0 billion to $82.0 billion.

Conference Call and Webcast Information

Supermicro will present a live audio webcast of our conference call to review its first quarter 2027 financial results on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. ET / 2:00 p.m. PT. The webcast will be available at https://ir.supermicro.com.

A replay of the webcast will be available shortly after the call at the same website and will remain accessible for one year.

Forward Looking Statements and Other Disclosures

Statements contained in this press release that are not historical fact may be forward looking statements within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933 and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. These forward-looking statements can be identified by the use of forward-looking terminology such as “anticipate,” “believe,” “continue,” “could,” “estimate,” “expect,” “may,” “plan,” “seek,” “should,” “will,” “would” “optimistic” or similar expressions and the negatives of those terms. Such forward looking statements may include statements regarding, among other things, guidance for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027. Such forward looking statements do not constitute guarantees of future performance and are subject to a variety of risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those anticipated, including: (i) our quarterly operating results may fluctuate, (ii) as we increasingly target larger customers and larger sales opportunities, our customer base may become more concentrated, our cost of sales may increase, our margins may be lower and our sales may become less predictable for a variety of reasons, many of which are not in our control, (iii) the average sales prices for our server solutions could decline if customers do not continue to purchase our latest generation products or additional components, and (iv) adverse economic conditions could affect our business, including, but not limited to, increased tariffs. Certain prior period amounts have been reclassified to conform to the current period presentation. Additional factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those projected or suggested in any forward-looking statements are detailed in our filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including those factors discussed under the caption “Risk Factors” in such filings, particularly in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for our fiscal year ended June 30, 2026.

Financial Information Is Preliminary and May Be Subject to Change

The unaudited financial information presented in this press release is preliminary. The final financial results reported for this period may also differ from the results reported in this release.

The financial results presented reflect the Company's preliminary estimated unaudited financial results, based upon information available to the Company as of the date of this press release. The Company has provided preliminary estimates of financial results primarily because its financial closing procedures for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 are not yet complete. The data are not a comprehensive statement of the Company's results for such periods, and the actual results may differ materially from these preliminary estimated data. The Company's actual results remain subject to the completion of management’s and its audit committee’s review and other financial closing processes as well as the completion and preparation of its financial data for such periods. The Company's independent registered public accounting firm has not audited, reviewed, compiled or performed any procedures with respect to such preliminary data. During the course of the preparation of the Company's financial statements and related notes and the completion of the review for such periods, additional adjustments to the preliminary estimated financial information presented here may be identified, and its final results for these periods may vary from these preliminary estimates. This preliminary estimated data should not be considered a substitute for the financial statements to be prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States and to be filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission once available.



About Super Micro Computer, Inc.

Supermicro (NASDAQ: SMCI) is a global leader in Application-Optimized Total IT Solutions. Founded and operating in San Jose, California, Supermicro is committed to delivering first-to-market innovation for Enterprise, Cloud, AI, and 5G/Edge IT Infrastructure. We are a Total IT Solutions provider with server, AI, storage, IoT, switch systems, software, and support services. Supermicro's motherboard, power, and chassis design expertise further enables our development and production, enabling next-generation innovation from cloud to edge for our global customers. Our products are designed and manufactured in-house (in the US, Taiwan, Malaysia, and the Netherlands), leveraging global operations for scale and efficiency and optimized to improve TCO and reduce environmental impact (Green Computing). The award-winning portfolio of Server Building Block Solutions® allows customers to optimize for their exact workload and application by selecting from a broad family of systems built from our flexible and reusable building blocks that support a comprehensive set of form factors, processors, memory, GPUs, storage, networking, power, and cooling solutions (air-conditioned, free air cooling, or liquid cooling).

Supermicro, Server Building Block Solutions, and We Keep IT Green are trademarks and/or registered trademarks of Super Micro Computer, Inc.

All other brands, names, and trademarks are the property of their respective owners.
